course_title: OCP Ready™ Data Center Recognition Program
course_subtitle: Learn how OCP Ready™ recognizes data centers prepared to support OCP infrastructure and solutions.
course_description_html:
This course explains the OCP Ready™ Data Center Recognition Program for colocation facilities. You’ll learn the two recognition paths, key site-assessment requirements, and the steps for preparing, submitting, and maintaining an OCP Ready™ recognition.


Click START COURSE or select a lesson below.

blocks.body_html:
OCP offers several logos and certification marks to members who show expertise in designing, deploying, and optimizing scalable, energy-efficient data center infrastructures.

We award these specific attributes through our OCP Solution Provider Program.

This program enables members to position their products, solutions, facilities, and services to meet the growing OCP market opportunity.
In this module, we'll provide a complete overview of the OCP Ready™ program, including its requirements, benefits, and the process for achieving the OCP Ready™ certification mark.

blocks.label: CONTINUE

blocks.body_html: Colocation data center operators participating in the OCP Ready™ Data Center Recognition Program perform a detailed OCP Ready™ self-assessment of their facilities to ensure they meet the rigorous standards and requirements set forth by the Data Center Facilities Project.

From logistics, site access, and base building infrastructure to network connectivity, every aspect of the data center is evaluated to confirm alignment with hyperscale facility requirements and compatibility with OCP and industry best practices. This enables colocation providers to market their facilities directly to the hyperscale audience.

Data Centers that meet the OCP Ready™ requirements and complete the process will receive an OCP Ready™ certification mark.

There are two self-certifications: OCP Ready™ v1 and OCP Ready™ v2 for Hyperscale.

Click each flipcard to learn more.

back.description_html: For data centers meeting OCP and industry best practices for high-density power, cooling, and physical infrastructure, optimized for OCP recognized hardware (e.g., Open Rack V2).

front.description_html: OCP Ready v2™ for Hyperscale

back.description_html: For data centers catering to hyperscale operators, emphasizing site security, logistics, base building infrastructure, and requiring MWs of power and cooling capacity for large-scale wholesale deployments.

blocks.body_html: The transition from OCP Ready™ v1 to OCP Ready™ v2 for Hyperscale reflects a shift towards multi-tenant data centers accommodating the larger scale, higher density, and more advanced infrastructure requirements of hyperscale operations.

blocks.body_html:
The OCP Ready™ program is unique in its focus on hyperscale-aligned requirements and its self-assessment model, which distinguishes it from other well-known data center certification programs. While all programs aim to validate data center reliability and operational excellence, their emphasis and methodology differ.

Let's take a look at how the OCP Ready™ program compares to two certification programs.

Click each tab to learn more.

items.title: Uptime Institute Tier Certification
items.description_html:
The Uptime Institute's Tier certification of a constructed facility is an evaluation of a data center's design, construction, and ongoing operations, verifying that the facility meets specific requirements for redundancy, fault tolerance, and operational sustainability.

Uptime's evaluation and certification is determined by on-site inspections by accredited third party consultants, which is in distinct contrast to the self-certified approach taken by the OCP Ready program.

items.title: TIA-942 (ANSI/TIA-942)
items.description_html: TIA-942 certification is based on compliance with the telecommunications infrastructure standard for data centers, defining design, construction, and operation requirements. The certification process requires a third-party auditor to assess and verify compliance with the standard’s requirements.

blocks.body_html:
Upon successful completion of the site assessment and approvals from the Data Center Facilities (DCF) Project Team and OCP Foundation, colocation data center operators will receive the designation as an OCP Ready™ v1 data center or OCP Ready™ v2 for Hyperscale data center, which is a testament to their commitment to innovation, efficiency, and sustainability.

OCP Ready™ data centers are listed on the OCP Marketplace and promoted through various OCP marketing activities. The OCP Ready™ recognition not only enhances the credibility and marketability of their facilities but also opens doors to new opportunities and partnerships within the hyperscale and enterprise ecosystems.

blocks.body_html: Click each step to learn how data centers are recognized as OCP Ready™.

items.description_html:
Members choose the data center site assessment that aligns with their data center design/specification and target market.

There are currently two versions of the site assessment:

  1. OCP Ready™ v2 for Hyperscale: For data centers catering to hyperscale operators, emphasizing site security, logistics, base building infrastructure, and MWs of power and cooling capacity for large-scale wholesale deployments.

  2. OCP Ready™ v1: For colocation data centers meeting OCP and industry best practices for high-density power, cooling, and physical infrastructure, optimized for OCP recognized hardware (e.g., Open Rack V2).

There is a site assessment required for each recognition:

  1. OCP Ready™ v2 for Hyperscale Data Center Site Assessment (Google Sheet) (Excel)

  2. OCP Ready™ v1 Data Center Site Assessment (Google Sheet) (Excel)
Potential members complete the site assessment and contact the OCP Ready™ Facilities Lead to review their submission and discuss next steps.
Once the OCP Ready™ Facilities Lead confirms the site assessment meets the requirements, they sign the required OCP Membership and Solution Provider agreements.

The member presents their completed data center site assessment to the Data Center Facility Community for final evaluation and approval.

The Data Center Facilities Project Leads, OCP Ready™ Facility Lead and the Foundation team are all involved in the approval of a data center.
Upon approval, the member executes the OCP Ready™ Certification Mark License Agreement and prepares promotional materials to be listed on the OCP Marketplace.
The member's data center is published on the OCP Marketplace, making it visible to a global audience.

The OCP Foundation team issues the OCP Ready™ logo and proof of self-certification, as well as ongoing quarterly OCP Marketplace Analytics and joint business development opportunities with the member.
